ai.literal: Even for love, is there a shutting bolt? The tears of distress of those who have affection will make a proclamation.
ai.translation: Is there any bolt that can lock up love? The tiny tears of distressed loved ones will loudly proclaim it.
ai.modern: அன்பை அடைத்து வைக்கக்கூடிய தாழ்ப்பாள் ஏதேனும் இருக்கிறதா? அன்பிற்குரியவர்களின் துன்பத்தைக் கண்டு பெருகும் கண்ணீரே அந்த அன்பை வெளிப்படுத்திவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the uncontrollable nature of true love. The poet asks rhetorically if there is any bolt or latch (தாழ்) that can confine or hide love (அன்பு). The answer is no, because when those we love are in distress, our own tears (புன்கணீர்) will immediately flow, acting as a loud proclamation (பூசல்) of our hidden affection. The word 'பூசல்' here means a loud announcement or clamor, showing how tears betray the secret of one's deep love.

ai.literal: Those who lack love, everything to themselves they claim; those who possess love, even their bones belong to others.
ai.translation: Those who lack love claim everything for themselves; those who possess love yield even their very bones to others.
ai.modern: அன்பு இல்லாதவர்கள் எல்லாப் பொருட்களையும் தமக்கே உரியதாகக் கொள்வர்; அன்பு உடையவர்கள் தம் உடம்பையும் பிறருக்கு உரியதாக்குவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the selfish nature of those who lack love with the ultimate selflessness of those who possess it. People without love seek to hoard everything, believing that all things belong solely to them. In stark contrast, those filled with love are so generous that they consider even their own physical bodies, represented here by bones, as belonging to others. The word 'enpu' (bone) is used metaphorically to signify the most fundamental, innermost part of one's physical existence, highlighting that true love knows no boundaries of self-preservation.

ai.literal: With-love conjoined way-of-life they-say, to-precious-life, with-bone conjoined connection.
ai.translation: They say that the connection of the precious soul with the bony body is for the purpose of leading a life conjoined with love.
ai.modern: அரிய உயிரானது உடம்போடு பொருந்தி இருப்பதன் தொடர்பு, அன்போடு கூடிய வாழ்க்கையை நடத்துவதற்கே என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the very purpose of human embodiment. The poet states that the union of the precious soul with the physical body of bones is meant for experiencing and practicing a life filled with love. The physical body is not just a material vessel, but an instrument designed specifically to express affection and kindness. Without love, the connection between the soul and the body loses its true meaning.

ai.literal: Love yields the possession of yearning; that yields the unsought excellence called friendship.
ai.translation: Love produces a yearning for connection with others, and that yearning yields the priceless, effortless excellence called friendship.
ai.modern: அன்பு பிறரிடம் விருப்பம் கொள்ளும் தன்மையைத் தரும்; அந்த விருப்பம் நட்பு என்று சொல்லப்படும் தேடாமலே கிடைக்கும் சிறந்த சிறப்பைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the beautiful progression of human relationships starting from love. Love (அன்பு) naturally gives rise to a deep yearning or desire (ஆர்வம்) to connect and be with others. This yearning, in turn, effortlessly yields the supreme excellence of friendship (நண்பு). The word 'நாடா' (unsought) highlights that true friendship is not something one has to laboriously search for; rather, it comes naturally and effortlessly to those who possess a loving heart.

ai.literal: The way of life associated with having obtained love, they say, is the excellence attained by those who obtained happiness in this world.
ai.translation: They say that a life lived in union with love is the source of the great distinction attained by those who enjoy happiness in this world.
ai.modern: இவ்வுலகில் இன்பம் அடைந்தவர்கள் பெறும் சிறப்பானது, அவர்கள் அன்போடு பொருந்தி வாழ்ந்த வாழ்க்கையின் பயனே என்று கூறுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the connection between love and worldly happiness. It states that the great distinction or excellence (சிறப்பு) enjoyed by those who are happy (இன்புற்றார்) in this world (வையகத்து) is actually the result of a life lived in harmony with love (அன்புற்று அமர்ந்த வழக்கு). Here, 'வழக்கு' refers to the conduct or path of life, and 'அமர்ந்த' means abiding or being established in. The poet emphasizes that true happiness and the honor that comes with it do not occur by chance, but are the direct fruits of practicing love in one's daily life.

ai.literal: Only to virtue love is a support, they say, those who do not know; even to valor, that itself is the support.
ai.translation: The ignorant say that love is a support only for virtue; but indeed, it is also the driving support for valor and overcoming hostility.
ai.modern: அன்பு அறத்திற்கு மட்டுமே சார்பு என்று அறிவில்லாதவர்கள் கூறுவார்கள்; வீரத்திற்கும் தீமையை எதிர்ப்பதற்கும் கூட அதுவே துணையாக இருக்கிறது.
ai.explanation: This couplet corrects a common misconception about the scope of love. Ignorant people believe that love is only useful for gentle, virtuous deeds. However, love is also the driving force behind valor or hostility, as one fights fiercely or opposes evil out of deep love for their family, country, or ideals. Thus, love serves as the ultimate foundation for both peaceful virtue and courageous action.

ai.literal: That which is without bone, the sun like, will scorch; that which is without love, righteousness [will scorch].
ai.translation: Just as the scorching sun burns up boneless creatures, so does Righteousness burn up those who are devoid of love.
ai.modern: எலும்பு இல்லாத உயிர்களை வெயில் சுட்டெரிப்பது போல, அன்பு இல்லாதவர்களை அறம் அழித்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid analogy from nature to illustrate the vital importance of love in human life. The 'boneless' creatures, such as worms, have no internal skeletal support to withstand the heat of the sun and are easily dried up and destroyed by it. Similarly, those who lack love have no inner moral strength, and 'Aṟam' (the cosmic principle of righteousness) will inevitably wither and ruin them. Love is thus presented as the essential backbone of human existence, without which one cannot survive the moral laws of the universe.

ai.literal: Love inside lacking life-existence, in a barren land, a withered tree sprouting is like.
ai.translation: The life of one who lacks love in their heart is like a withered tree trying to sprout in a barren desert.
ai.modern: மனதில் அன்பு இல்லாதவருடைய வாழ்க்கை, வறண்ட பாலைநிலத்தில் காய்ந்துபோன மரம் தளிர்ப்பது போன்றதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a vivid metaphor from nature to describe the futility of a life lived without love. The poet compares a person whose heart is devoid of love (அன்பகத்து இல்லா) to a completely dried-up, withered tree (வற்றல் மரம்) standing in a harsh, barren desert (வன்பாற்கண்). Just as it is impossible for such a dead tree to sprout fresh green leaves (தளிர்த்தற்று) in a waterless wasteland, it is impossible for someone without love to flourish or experience a meaningful, fruitful life. The key words 'வன்பால்' (barren land) and 'வற்றல் மரம்' (withered tree) emphasize that love is the essential life-force, without which all outward efforts at living are utterly in vain.

ai.literal: External limbs all what use will they do to the body, if the internal limb, love, to those who lack?
ai.translation: Of what use are all the outer limbs of the body to those who lack the inner limb of love?
ai.modern: உள்ளத்து உறுப்பாகிய அன்பு இல்லாதவர்களுக்கு, உடம்பின் வெளி உறுப்புகள் எல்லாம் என்ன பயனைச் செய்யும்?
ai.explanation: This couplet compares love to an essential internal organ (அகத்துறுப்பு) of the body, while the physical limbs (like hands, eyes, and legs) are merely external organs (புறத்துறுப்பு). Just as a body cannot truly live or function without its vital internal organs, a human life is meaningless without the inner quality of love. For those who lack love in their hearts, having all external limbs intact is of no real value, as they cannot perform genuine acts of human connection. The poet uses the archaic verb form 'செய்பும்' to ask what useful action these outer limbs could possibly perform without the guiding force of love.

ai.literal: The seat of life is of the path of love; for those who lack that, the body is bone covered with skin.
ai.translation: A living body is one that walks the path of love; for those who lack love, their body is merely bones clad in skin.
ai.modern: அன்பின் வழியில் இயங்குவதே உயிருள்ள உடம்பாகும்; அன்பு இல்லாதவர்களுடைய உடம்பு வெறும் தோலால் மூடப்பட்ட எலும்பு மட்டுமே ஆகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the vital importance of love in defining true human existence. The author states that a body is truly alive only when it is guided by love. Without love, a person's physical form is nothing more than a lifeless skeleton wrapped in skin. The key contrast is between 'உயிர்நிலை' (the true seat of life) and a mere 'உடம்பு' (a physical body of bone and skin), showing that love is the animating force of human life.
